item.title: Hezbollah rocket hits Kiryat Shmona without warning sirens as Lebanon war intensifies
item.description:
A Hezbollah rocket struck a residential area of Kiryat Shmona on Saturday without warning sirens activating, damaging buildings and infrastructure in the northern Israeli border town, as cross-border fighting between Israel and the Lebanese militant group intensified on multiple axes.

The strike, which caused no reported casualties, prompted an investigation by the Israel Defense Forces into the failure of its alert systems. It came amid a day of sustained Hezbollah barrages targeting northern Israeli communities, with the group claiming it hit Kiryat Shmona at least seven times on Friday alone using rockets and loitering drones. Hezbollah also claimed attacks on Israeli troop concentrations in the border towns of Marun al-Ras, Hula, Ainata, and Bayada in southern Lebanon.

item.title: Russia evacuates 198 workers after strike near Iran's Bushehr nuclear plant kills one
item.description: A projectile struck near Iran's Bushehr nuclear power plant on Saturday morning, killing a security guard and damaging an auxiliary building in what the International Atomic Energy Agency confirmed was the fourth such incident since the US-Israeli military campaign against Iran began on February 28.

item.title: Jerusalem's Old City marks quiet Easter as Iran war enters sixth week
item.description: Jerusalem's Old City, normally bustling with pilgrims and tourists during the spring holiday season, has fallen nearly silent as Passover and Easter coincide under the shadow of the ongoing war between Iran and the U.S.-Israeli coalition. Metal shutters line the stone alleyways, holy sites stand largely empty, and the few worshippers who come do so under strict military guidelines that have transformed one of the world's most sacred quarters into a ghost town.

item.title: Drone strikes wound 3 at BP-run oilfield in Iraq
item.description: Two drones struck the BP-operated North Rumaila oilfield in southern Iraq on Saturday, wounding three Iraqi workers, as a separate drone targeted offices belonging to American energy services company KBR at the nearby Majnoon oil field, underscoring the continued vulnerability of Iraq's energy infrastructure more than a month into the broader conflict between the United States, Israel, and Iran.

item.title: Iran launches 95th wave of strikes on U.S. bases across Gulf
item.description: Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps carried out a sweeping series of strikes on Saturday targeting U.S. military positions in Kuwait, Bahrain, and the United Arab Emirates, marking the 95th wave of Operation True Promise 4 since the war began five weeks ago. The Iranian Navy also claimed to have set ablaze an Israeli-linked commercial vessel near the Strait of Hormuz.

item.title: Houthis claim joint strike with Iran on Ben Gurion Airport
item.description:
Yemen's Houthi movement claimed Saturday that it struck Ben Gurion Airport near Tel Aviv and military targets in southern Israel using a fragmentation ballistic missile and attack drones, in what the group described as a joint operation with Iran's Revolutionary Guard, the Iranian army, and Hezbollah in Lebanon.

Houthi military spokesperson Yahya Saree said in a prerecorded statement that the group had "successfully struck Lod Airport (Ben Gurion) in the occupied Jaffa area" along with what he called vital military targets in southern occupied Palestine. "This operation was a joint operation with the Revolutionary Guard, the Iranian army, and Hezbollah in Lebanon, and it successfully achieved its objectives," Saree said.

item.title: Israel warns it will strike Lebanon-Syria border crossing
item.description: The Israel Defense Forces carried out simultaneous waves of strikes across Iran and Lebanon over the weekend, hitting more than 200 Iranian targets and over 140 Hezbollah positions as the five-week-old Operation Roaring Lion continued to expand in scope. The IDF also confirmed the death of another soldier in southern Lebanon, bringing the toll to 11 since ground operations began on March 16.

item.title: Trump aides advise striking Iran's infrastructure as Monday deadline nears
item.description:
Senior Trump administration officials have privately advised President Donald Trump that striking Iran's energy and power infrastructure constitutes a legitimate military target, according to The Wall Street Journal, as the U.S.-Iran war enters its sixth week with a critical deadline just two days away.

The reporting comes as Trump's self-imposed April 6 deadline for Iran to reopen the Strait of Hormuz or reach a deal approaches on Monday evening. On Saturday, Trump reiterated his ultimatum on Truth Social, warning that "all hell" would rain down on Iran if it fails to comply within 48 hours.

item.title: Trump warns Iran of 'hell' as search for downed jet crew enters day 2
item.description: President Donald Trump dismissed the loss of an American F-15E Strike Eagle fighter jet over Iran on Friday, telling NBC News in a phone interview that the incident would have no bearing on ongoing diplomatic efforts with Tehran. "No, not at all. No, it's war. We're in war, Garrett," Trump told NBC News correspondent Garrett Haake, in his first public remarks on the shootdown.

item.title: Iran's grip on Strait of Hormuz fuels growing recession fears worldwide
item.description: A grinding war in Iran and the effective closure of the Strait of Hormuz have sent oil prices surging and rattled financial markets worldwide, intensifying fears that the global economy may be headed for a recession. With crude benchmarks trading well above $100 a barrel and bond yields falling, Wall Street is signaling that the risk of economic contraction now outweighs concerns about inflation.

item.title: Iran's military warns Israeli embassies are 'legitimate targets'
item.description: Iran's top military command issued a stark warning on Saturday that any Israeli attack on Iranian embassies or diplomatic facilities would prompt retaliatory strikes on Israeli diplomatic sites across the Middle East, escalating rhetoric amid an ongoing military conflict between Iran and a US-Israeli coalition.

item.title: Meloni offers to help rebuild Qatar's war-damaged gas infrastructure
item.description:
Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni met with Qatari Emir Sheikh Tamim bin Hamad Al Thani at Lusail Palace in Doha on Saturday, offering Italy's support to rebuild Qatar's damaged energy infrastructure as Europe grapples with an energy crisis triggered by the US-Israeli war on Iran.

Meloni is the first leader from the European Union, NATO, and the G20 to visit the Gulf region since the conflict began on February 28. The unannounced two-day tour, which started in Saudi Arabia on Friday with a meeting with Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, will also include the United Arab Emirates.

item.title: Iran rejects Trump's 48-hour ultimatum as Gulf strikes widen
item.description:
Iran's central military command on Saturday dismissed President Donald Trump's 48-hour ultimatum to reopen the Strait of Hormuz or face the destruction of its critical infrastructure, as Tehran continued launching waves of drone and missile strikes across the Gulf and at Israel in the latest escalation of the five-week-old war.

General Ali Abdollahi Aliabadi, representing Iran's Khatam al-Anbiya Central Headquarters, called Trump's threat "a helpless, nervous, unbalanced and stupid action," and warned: "The simple meaning of this message is that the gates of hell will open for you." Trump had written on Truth Social earlier Saturday: "Time is running out — 48 hours before all Hell will reign down on them. Glory be to GOD!"

item.title: Israel strikes Iran's petrochemical zone as US pilot search continues
item.description: U.S. and Israeli warplanes struck Iran's Mahshahr Special Petrochemical Zone on Saturday, killing at least five people and wounding 170 others according to Iranian state media, as the search for a missing American crew member whose fighter jet was shot down the previous day stretched into a second day.

item.title: U.S. forces rescue second F-15E crew member from Iran after firefight
item.description:
U.S. military forces successfully extracted the second crew member of an F-15E Strike Eagle that was shot down over Iran on Friday, capping a tense rescue operation that stretched more than 24 hours and involved firefights with Iranian forces on the ground, according to U.S. officials cited by The Wall Street Journal.

The weapons systems officer had been evading capture in southwestern Iran while Iranian military units and local militia forces combed the area, with Iranian state media broadcasting a bounty of roughly $60,000 for anyone who located the American airmen, according to the BBC. U.S. special operations forces reached the WSO and extracted him in what journalist Jack Murphy, a former Green Beret, described as a "massive firefight" at the recovery site. Al Jazeera reported that a U.S. government representative confirmed the second crew member had been "retrieved" after an "intense exchange of gunfire".

item.title: Iranian drones hit Kuwait government, oil buildings in latest Gulf strikes
item.description: Kuwait, Saudi Arabia, Bahrain, and other Persian Gulf nations endured another wave of Iranian drone and missile attacks over the weekend, as the US-Israeli military campaign against Iran stretches into its sixth week with no end in sight.

item.title: Western carriers seize routes as Iran war guts Gulf aviation hubs
item.description: More than five weeks after the United States and Israel launched strikes on Iran on February 28, the war has upended the global aviation industry, shuttering Middle Eastern airspace, grounding tens of thousands of flights, and opening a rare window for Western and Turkish carriers to capture traffic long dominated by Gulf airlines.

item.title: Pope Leo XIV celebrates Easter Mass at the Vatican
item.description: Christians around the world are marking Easter Sunday on April 5, 2026, with religious services, community gatherings, and festive celebrations commemorating the resurrection of Jesus Christ.

item.title: Pope Leo XIV to deliver first Urbi et Orbi amid war critique
item.description: Pope Leo XIV has used the solemn liturgies of Holy Week to deliver a sustained rebuke of those who invoke Christianity to justify military action, drawing a sharp contrast with U.S. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth's calls to pray for battlefield triumph "in the name of Jesus Christ."

item.title: Pope Leo XIV leads first Easter Vigil with plea for peace
item.description: Pope Leo XIV presided over his first Easter Vigil as pontiff on Saturday evening at St. Peter's Basilica, delivering a homily that urged the world not to grow numb to war and called on the faithful to help the "Easter gifts of harmony and peace" take root across the globe.
